_meta.authors: Audrey Hategekimana (schemas, mapping, serialisation notes) with review from Akuzwe Anny Benitha (sample values checked against the SMS export)
_meta.purpose: JSON representations of the database entities, showing how relational rows are serialised for API responses.
_meta.source_of_values: All sample values are copied from data/raw/modified_sms_v2.xml or from the rows inserted by database/02_seed_data.sql. Nothing here is invented.

json_schemas._note: Draft-07 schemas for each entity. These are the contract: every enum list below matches the SQL ENUM exactly, so a payload the API rejects is a payload MySQL would also have rejected. The entity_examples further down are all validated against these.

phone_number.description: Either a full MSISDN or the masked form the SMS supplied. Internal endpoints only — public responses carry phone_masked instead.

participant.title: Participant
participant.description: One row of Transaction_Participants after the junction has been flattened. participant_id is dropped and user_id is replaced by the user object.

raw_sms_body.description: Detail endpoint only. Holds names, account numbers and balances, so list responses drop it.

sql_to_json_mapping._note: Column-by-column mapping between the MySQL schema and its JSON form. Junction tables do not appear as top-level objects: the relationship they carry is expressed in JSON by nesting instead.

columns.phone_number: phone_number on internal endpoints; replaced by phone_masked on public ones, matching the v_transactions_masked view

columns.financial_transaction_id: financial_transaction_id (string or null — null on 52% of messages)
columns.category_id: replaced by the embedded category object

Transaction_Participants.json_object: none, flattened into the participants array of a transaction

columns.participant_id: omitted, it is an internal surrogate key with no API meaning
columns.transaction_id: implied by position inside the parent transaction
columns.user_id: replaced by the embedded user object

columns.transaction_id: omitted when nested inside a transaction, present as transaction_id when returned standalone

entity_examples._note: One flat example per entity: a single row serialised on its own, with foreign keys left as raw ids. Each validates against the matching schema above.

category.name: Transfer Received
category.description: Peer-to-peer money received ("You have received X RWF from ...")

user_with_masked_number._note: Jane Smith's number was masked in the source SMS as (*********013). The masked form is stored verbatim rather than guessed at, which is different from the number being unknown.

transaction_flat._note: The list-view shape: no nesting, no raw message text.

log_entry_unlinked._note: transaction_id is null because this message never became a transaction.
log_entry_unlinked.message: Skipped OTP SMS: not a financial transaction

_note: A complete transaction with all related data nested, built from a real message:
*165*S*10000 RWF transferred to Samuel Carter (250791666666) from 36521838 at
2024-05-11 20:34:47 . Fee was: 100 RWF. New balance: 28300 RWF.
Chosen because it has a non-zero fee, an unmasked phone number and two
participants in different roles, so the nested participants array actually
demonstrates the M:N resolution rather than looking decorative. It also has
no transaction id at all, which is why financial_transaction_id is null here
and why that column is not the primary key.
Three nesting techniques are at work: category_id becomes an embedded
object, the junction table becomes an array of objects, and each
participant embeds the full user plus its role.

complex_transaction_three_party._note: A second complex object showing why the junction table was worth the extra complexity. This agent withdrawal has the account owner and the agent in different roles on a single message, and a sender_id/receiver_id column pair could not have held both plus the till. It is also the only sample row with a fee above 300 RWF, which is what makes agent cash-out visibly expensive in the fee report.

api_response_examples._note: Realistic API envelopes. List endpoints trim raw_sms_body and processing_logs to keep payloads small, and swap phone_number for phone_masked; the detail endpoint returns everything to an authenticated internal caller.

GET /api/transactions/4.data: the full complex_transaction object above, including raw_sms_body and processing_logs

GET /api/users/3/transactions._note: The user object is hoisted to the top level rather than repeated inside every participant array, since it is the same user on every row.

GET /api/categories/summary._note: Reads v_monthly_summary, so the arithmetic happens in MySQL. Figures match query C1 in 04_crud_and_tests.sql.

error_response_422._note: A CHECK constraint or trigger failure is translated into a structured validation error rather than letting the raw SQLSTATE reach the client.

error.message: The transaction could not be saved

details.message: amount must be zero or greater

serialisation_design_notes: DECIMAL columns are serialised as strings, not JSON numbers. JSON has no fixed-point type, and a client that reads 10000.00 into a double will eventually disagree with the database about a total. Strings push the decision to the client, which can parse them with a decimal library. The alternative — integer minor units — works too, but RWF has no subunit in practice, so strings read more naturally.
DATETIME becomes an ISO 8601 string with the +02:00 Africa/Kigali offset attached. MySQL stores these naive, so without the offset a client in another zone would silently shift every timestamp.

ENUM columns become plain strings, in the same upper case the database uses. The JSON Schema enum lists mirror the SQL ENUM lists exactly, so a value the API rejects is a value MySQL would also have rejected — one rule, enforced in two places.

Nulls are kept explicit rather than omitted. A null financial_transaction_id is meaningful: it records that the source SMS carried no transaction id, which happens on 868 of the 1,691 messages and is different from the field being absent.

The Transaction_Participants junction table has no JSON counterpart. Its rows become the participants array, and participant_id is dropped entirely since it is an internal surrogate key with no meaning to an API consumer.

phone_number never leaves the API on a public endpoint. Responses carry phone_masked instead, which is the same substitution the v_transactions_masked view makes in the database, so the privacy rule holds whether a client reads through the API or straight from the dashboard view.
List endpoints omit raw_sms_body and processing_logs. Across the full corpus the raw text would dominate the payload, and clients browsing a list do not need it.
Nesting depth is capped at three levels (transaction, participants, user). Deeper would mean a user object containing its own transactions, which recurses without end.
